title: Divers Find What May Be the World’s Oldest Shipwreck
paragraphs: Researchers say a shipwreck in shallow water off Kekova, west of Antalya in Turkey, may be the oldest in the world. They think it sank about 4,500 years ago.

Hakan Öniz of Akdeniz University found the site in 2024 after local sailors gave him clues. The wooden ship is gone, but large clay jars called amphorae remain on a rocky slope. Divers spent about four months taking them off the rocks.

The jars may have held olive oil, wine or tree resin, but tests are not finished. Some jars, or the clay, may come from the Jordan Valley. The report is not yet checked by other scientists, so the date could change.

questions.a: Only the clay jars; the wood is gone.
Other scientists have not checked the report yet.
